maintopic: INTER-IMPERIAL TRADE.
INTER-IMPERIAL TRADE.
speechtext:
Before the Orders of the Day are called, I would like to draw the attention of the
Prime Minister to a cable which appears in the London Times of May 2nd from its Australian correspondent. The cable reads as follows :-
Melbourne, May 1.-Mr. Muloek, the Canadian Postmaster General, is empowered to conler with the Federal government and with a view to adoption of an Imperial tariff policy, preferential duties being mutually allowed between Great Britain, the Dominion, the comjnonwealth and1 the colonies generally. Mr. Muloek thinks there' is considerable room for an increase of trade between Canada and Australia.
I would like to ask the Prime Minister as to the accuracy of the statement in that cablegram and whether, on leaving Canada, Mr. Muloek received instructions to enter into negotiations with the Australian Commonwealth, the Dominion and the mother country. Any information the Prime Minister can give the House and the country, I am sure, will be received with a great deal of interest.

maintopic: INTER-IMPERIAL TRADE.
speechtext: I may say to my hon. friend (Mr. Clarke) and the House that Mr. Mul-ock is the bearer of no specific formal instructions. But he has received informal instructions to ascertain to what extent it would be possible to promote trade between Canada and Australia and to make a report upon the subject on his return.
speakername: The PRIME MINISTER (Rt. Hon. Sir Wilfrid Laurier).

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.

speechtext:
Bill (No. 138) to provide for a further annual allowance for the province of Prince Edward Island (Hon. Mr. Fielding), read the second time and House went into committee thereon.
On section 1,

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: In connection with this matter I would like to ask the Minister of Finance to tell the House and the country now whether any other claims of the provinces for better terms have been filed, and of what nature they are.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: I do not regard this as a claim for better terms, therefore my hon. friend's remark about any other claims for better terms is calculated to mislead.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Then are there any claims from any of the provinces ? We are laying down a principle here, we have opened the door again. We are taking up one case, others are to follow. Now I would like the minister to tell the House and the country what those other claims are that have been made on the government from different provinces of this confederation, if any.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
I think I can say that at the present moment there

is no claim from any of the provinces which is being made the subject of any very serious consideration. The various provinces from time to time have correspondence with us on matters of account and otherwise, but I would not like to treat these as serious claims. So far as the government is concerned, I think I am correct in stating that at the present time there is no claim from any of the provinces which the government are seriously entertaining, or which they contemplate submitting to parliament. The province of Prince Edward Island, and for that matter the maritime provinces generally, have from time to time advanced a claim on account of the fisheries award. It was represented that that award was peculiarly the property of the lower provinces, and should have been paid over to them. That matter, in one form or another, has been before parliament for twenty years, or for a very long period, and I have no doubt that for twenty years to come somebody will be found to advocate such a view. The province of Prince Edward Island recently referred to that in the course of representations by a delegation, and dwelt upon the fact that by reason of a decision of the courts the rights of the provinces in these fisheries have become much stronger than they were before. Our answer to that was that in connection with the fishery award, if not directly arising out of that, there was the grant of the fishing bounty, and we have gently intimated to the provinces that if they should see fit to test their possible technical legal rights in the matter of this fishery award, they would also have to take account of the fishery bounty winch the parliament of Canada grants. They could not expect to get the money and get the bounty also; and therefore, I assume that that question is not likely to be seriously presented. At all events, if it should be presented, I do not hestiate to say that they cannot claim to be repaid the amount of the jaward and at the same time receive the fishing bounty. Therefore. I do not treat that as a very serious matter.
Then there was a claim-I am speaking entirely from memory-there has been a claim standing for many years from the province of Manitoba, that is to say, they regard it as a claim. There was a sum of $110,000 at one time placed to the credit of Manitoba, but in subsequent legislation that sum was wiped out and other provisions made in lieu thereof, and covering, as we think, that amount. The province of Manitoba several years ago brought that up and insisted that the later legislation had not wiped out the $110,000. We considered that matter, and this government declined to recognize the claim. They had also another claim arising out of the construction of public buildings in Manitoba that we did recognize, and provided for some three years ago. The other claim this government refused to entertain. Within the last few Mr. FIELDING'.
months it has been brought forward again by the government of Manitoba, but we have nothing new to communicate to the House. We have not officially given the government of Manitoba an answer, but we shall be able to do so very quickly ; but I know no reason why we should depart from the conclusion previously reached. Now I believe I have mentioned all the claims from the maritime provinces, concerning which I have any knowledge.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Now what about Nova Scotia.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Nova Scotia has made no claim for better terms, and speaking, not by any authority, but for myself as a representative from the province of Nova Scotia, I will engage that no claim should be advanced by Nova Scotia by reason of this grant to Prince Edward Island. I will undertake to say that I will not myself support any claim that might be made, if it should be made by the government of Nova Scotia, by reason of this grant to the province of Prince Edward Island. I think this grant stands upon its own merits, and should not be mixed up with any question of other claims or of better terms.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
With respect to the fisheries matter which the hon. gentleman referred to, it is not correct to speak of it as a claim made by one of the provinces, or by a number of the provinces ; it is a contention as to the construction of the Act. It is a legal contention, that legal contention was submitted to parliament in the year, I think, 1880, by the then hon. member for Halifax, Mr. Richey, when Sir John A. Macdonald returned to power, and it was passed upon by parliament adversely to the contention of the province. That contention has been floating more or less in the air since parliament passed upon it at that time. That claim remained quiescent, but was revived by the decision of the Privy Council, which seemed to give some colour to the contention of the provinces with regard to their jurisdiction extending territorially over the three mile belt. Whether it does or does not, has not yet been decided ; but if eventually it is decided by the Privy Council that the contention of the maritime provinces with respect to their jurisdiction is as sound as they make it, even then if parliament did yield to their claim it would only be on the ground that my hon. friend has referred to, that the capital sum which Is now placed to their credit, and upon which they are receiving interest in the shape of bounties, being the amount awarded by the Halifax International tribunal, should cease to be paid to them afterwards. If they got the principal they could not get the interest in the shape of bounty, that would be perfecly clear, I take it. Therefore, it is not fair to speak of it as a claim ; it is more in the nature of a contention they make with regard to the

legal construction of tlieir rights under the British North America Act, and that never will be decided nor can be decided by any government until the Privy Council positively passes upon the matter again ; and Hf it is decided it must be decided on the lines my hon. friend the Minister of Finance states, that if they get the principal they certainly cannot get the interest which they are now getting in the shape of bounties.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Is there any complaint from the province of Ontario with regard to those bounties ?

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: The province of Ontario has no connection with it at all.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: I ask the Minister of Finance, as he was speaking about the other provinces, if any claim has been made respecting a readjustment of the sums paid to the provinces ?

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: No claim has been made from any of the provinces respecting a readjustment of its subsidy.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Or of any kind ?

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: I know of nothing from the province of Ontario.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: We are opening the door now. The hon. gentleman's own supporters 'behind him have said they intend to file their claims. The member for Labelle (Mr. Bourassa) filed a claim on behalf of the province of Quebec five minutes after this grant to Prince Edward Island was proposed. I believe that other claims will be filed now, and no doubt there are a number of claims.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: To relieve the suspicions of my hon. friend (Mr. Maclean) I may say that they are all groundless, and that all the claims that have been made up to this date are in the hands of the Governor General.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
Does the Minister of Marine and Fisheries (Hon. Sir Louis Davies) say that there is something to be determined in respect to the rights of the Dominion in the fisheries ?
The MINISTER OF MARINE	AND
FISHERIES. Yes, I say that there is still open the question as to the extent of the jurisdiction, or the territorial rights of the provinces over the three-mile belt. The provinces contend that as a result of the fisheries decision they are entitled to territorial jurisdiction over the three-mile belt.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
Has anything been done to settle that question ?
The MINISTER OF MARINE	AND
FISHERIES. Yes, we have been trying for some time to settle upon a case, and I think we have reached a reasonable settlement. The Premier of Quebec, the Attorney General of Quebec, the Deputy Minister of Justice and myself were in consultation a long time over it, and we have reached a conclusion which has been formulated in writing and which I have since transmitted to the Premier of Quebec. We have given instructions to our fishery officers in accordance with it. The Federal government will grant a license to fish in the disputed territory, and the provincial government will remove the nets. That will raise the question, and it will be brought into court for a decision. We will ask the court to decide whether we have territorial rights or not.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
When the matter of these resolutions was first brought before the House, attention was called to the fact that a tax was placed by the authorities in Prince Edward Island

the provincial authorities, I believe-upon commercial travellers from other provinces who desired to enter that province for the purpose of doing business, and I read a strong protest from the president of the Commercial Travellers' Association of Canada against the continuation of that tax. I was not sure, myself, when the matter was up, whether the tax was imposed by the municipalities or by the province.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: By the province.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: I thank the hon. gentleman. Then, I believe, I am correct in saying that the tax was levied by the province. This is a matter that causes a good deal of irritation and annoyance to the representatives of the business interests of other provinces, and it was brought to the attention of the government when these resolutions were presented by the Minister of Finance (Hon. Mr. Fielding). May I ask if any correspondence has taken place between the government of Prince Edward Island and the hon. gentleman respecting the remission of this tax ? I understand that representations have been made as to the unfairness of this tax. I do not desire to take up the time of the committee any farther than to ask if any correspondence has taken place in regard to the remission of this tax. and if not. would the government take steps as soon as possible to procure its removal ?

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: No correspondence has taken place between myself and the provincial government, but the hon. Minister of Justice, in the discharge of his duties as Minister of Justice, in respect to the legislation of the provinces, has called the attention of the provincial government to the complaints which have been made in respect to this legislation. The provincial government revised their legislation in this respect, and the legislature passed a new statute last session. I have not yet seen the statute, further than a newspaper comment upon it, but that new statute will come before the hon. Minister of Justice for his consideration.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: May I ask the hon. gentleman If there Is any intention under that new statute to increase these imposts ? The statement was made by the president of the Commercial Travellers' Association that he understood that the tax was increased from $15, or $25, to $50.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: I cannot give the hon. gentleman the details, but there has been a readjustment of the tax levied. I do not know exactly the extent of it, but perhaps my hon. friend may be right. The contention of the provincial government was that they were levying this tax for provincial purposes and that really they were not discriminating inasmuch as those carrying on the same business, being residents, paid an equivalent tax in what is called a pedlar's license there. I am not in a position to pronounce any judgment now one way or the other, but the matter is engaging the close attention of the hon. Minister of Justice.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Is it the intention to make any representations to the provincial government to secure a remission of this tax ?

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: The Minister of Justice is now in communication with the province, and until he receives the new statute which was passed last session, it is quite impossible to give any information one way or the other.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: It may be that the Act was ultra vires of that province. It is certainly a violation of the original compact of this confederation that one province should pass such legislation interfering with trade, and I think the government will find that it is ultra vires, or, at least, that it is in violation of the original contract of confederation, and so, I think, we are entitled, either through a decision of the courts, or by the persuasion of the government, to have it done away with.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: If I understood the hon. Minister of Marine and Fisheries rightly, there has been a renewal of the application which was made in parliament by Mr. Richey in 1880, I think, claiming $5,500,000.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: I think I may have misled the hon. gentleman if I said that there was a renewal. What I intended to say was that there was some revival of this old claim following the fisheries decision.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Since the fisheries decision by which jurisdiction over the three-mile limit was given to the provinces, there has been a revival of the claim put forward by Mr. Richey in this House for $5,500,000, the amount of the Washington award.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: That included the sum paid to Newfoundland.
speakername: The MINISTER OF TRADE AND COMMERCE (Hon. Sir Richard Cartwright).

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
That was $500,-
000.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: No, $1,000,000 W'as given to Newfoundland. I may say that the revival of this claim since the decision has not been made by the three or four provinces interested. It has only been intimated by one of the provinces that the claim was alive. The whole of the provinces have not made a claim, and I do not know that they intend it.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: All I am stating is that from the remarks of the hon. Minister of Marine and Fisheries, I understand that there has been a revival of this claim.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: By one province.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: As I understand him, by one province. Does the hon. gentleman remember the exact amount'! I think it was about

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: $4,500,000. We came to the conclusion that by distributing the award in the shape of bounties to the fishermen in the maritime provinces we were giving them adequate compensation. There was a claim made by New Brunswick against the government of the Dominion, and if I understand the hon. Minister of Finance, this claim has been settled. What is the amount that has been awarded ?

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: I do not recollect the exact amount, but it is about $250,000. That was under the award which was laid before the House! some time ago. Before the session closes we shall have to provide for dealing with these claims. As to the particular manner in which they will be dealt with I am not prepared to say, but that and the Nova Scotia award will be brought before the House before the close of the session.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: I understand the hon. Minister of Finance to say that the papers of the New Brunswick award have been laid before the House. We have not had the papers in regard to the Nova Scotia award.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: I am under the impression that the others were asked for and were also brought down. If not, I shall see that they are brought down.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: How many awards were there ?

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: There were two awards, that of New Brunswick, to which the hon. gentleman (Hon. Mr. Hag-gart) refers, and that of Nova Scotia.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
I would like to ask the hon. Minister of Finance by what means

the government are able to determine the amount that should be paid to Prince Edward Island, if anything. It is a matter of some importance that the committee should know the basis upon which this sum is granted. The hon. gentleman knows very well that the contentions of Prince Edward Island could not be fairly viewed and settled upon in the light of what we have before us to-day. I am not going to detain the committee except for one moment, and it is not for the purpose at all of trying to show that this is not an equitable claim. It may be an equitable claim, but what I want to call the hon. gentleman's attention to is that if Prince Edward Island's claim is based mainly upon the conditions as we find them to-day, the complete change in all the circumstances would make it appear very large. The people of Prince Edward Island themselves admitted that it was quite possible they would have to abandon the notion of a winter service, and they advocated the building of a tunnel, which of course was not contemplated in the terms of union. The House should have more than a general statement that the government have consented to give Prince Edward Island practically the interest on a million dollars for all time. In view of the conflicting opinions on the subject, we should be told bow the government arrived at that conclusion.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: I am afraid I cannot add anything to what has already been stated in debate, and in the order in council. It was not a matter of mathematical calculation to ascertain the precise cent to which the province was entitled. It was a conclusion reached by the government after a general review of the whole matter, we believing that it would probably be better for all interests, and, perhaps, better for the treasury of the Dominion, to make this allowance rather than to open up the question by way of arbitration which the Island government asked. We were of opinion that all interests would be better served by giving them this sum, not specially adjusted, but as an allowance in the way stated, in preference to entering into a general distribution, which might, perhaps, have given them less, or which, perhaps, might give them a good deal more.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: It occurs to me that in fixing this amount, there must have been some basis which guided the government. I do not say that the amount is too large or too little, but. I think the order in council might have shown what the basis *was. and that the Minister of Finance might have been able to explain it to the House. Any explanation that has been made from the Treasury benches in regard to this would sound equally well if you put in $20,000 or $40,000 instead of $30,000.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Quite so.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: It looks very much as if the amount were simply determined by what is called the rule of thumb, instead of being determined upon some definite principle. I dare say it may be difficult to find a basis on which to settle such a claim by compromise, but it seems to me there must have been some principle in the minds of the sub-committee who settled the claim, and the House ought to be apprised of it. However, it does not appear that the government are able to give us any information on that point, and I suppose we will have to be content without it. I have one other observation. If there is any other claim of thevprovince in respect to alleged violation of the compact between the Dominion and the province, it seems to me it would he very desirable to make an end of all such claims.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: There is no question outstanding respecting the terms of union, but the one touched by this Bill.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
The reason I supposed there was, is on account of the very definite language of the Bill, which says this is to be :
Accepted in full settlement of all claims of the said province against the Dominion of Canada on account of alleged nonfulfilment of the terms of union between the Dominion and the said province as respects the maintenance of efficient steam communication between the island and the mainland.
I supposed on account of that language, that there was some other claim or possible claim by the province of Prince Edward Island against Canada, and if so, I think the hon. gentleman (Mr. Fielding) will agree with me that it would be exceedingly desirable that any such claim should be dealt with now, so that we might not have friction and irritation with respect to such matters in the future. Certainly, the form in which the Act is presented to the House leaves it open to the province at any future time to make claims based on any consideration other than that expressed in this Bill.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
As to any other claim for nonfulfilment of the terms of union, T quite agree it should be covered by this Bill. I can say to my hon. friend without the slightest reservation- I am willing that my words should go down as forming part of the understanding- that this Bill covers all such claims. There is no claim by the government of Prince Edward Island with respect to the nonfulfilment of the terms of union other than this claim with regard to winter service. They have advanced other claims on matters of account, and the fisheries and so on, but, as respects any claim for nonfulfilment of the terms of union, this has been the only matter of controversy. There-

fore, the language used, which is the language of our correspendence with them, covers everything of that character without the slightest reservation.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: While the Minister of Finance says it covers all the matters in dispute so far as the terms of confederation are concerned, yet, the language of the Act is a direct invitation to the Island of Prince Edward to prefer its further claims. We know, and the Minister of Finance knows better than any of us, what these further claims are. There are claims because a large sum of money was spent by the Dominion in the construction of the Canadian Pacific Railway in which the government of the province allege they had no direct benefit. There are claims on account of the construction of the Prince Edward Island Railway. Therefore, when the government come here with their proposal to hand over virtually the interest on a million dollars to Prince Edward Island for all time to come in order to satisfy them, let me ask : Does the Minister of Marine (Hon. Sir Louis Davies) tell us that there was a nonfulfilment of the terms of the union in respect to steam communication ? The government do not say so in their Bill. They say on account of ' alleged ' nonfulnlment.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: W'e are very cautious.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Yes. but you are voting away a million dollars which does not show so much caution.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Oh. yes ; it does. It might have to be two millions.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Of course, this government, which is squandering our money and slinging it out in every direction, do not care for a million dollars, and they would just as soon make it two millions.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Election pledges.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
Yes, these pledges were made before the election, and they were made at the by-election the other day. At the general election a Conservative was returned, and a few weeks afterwards a supporter of the government was elected by hundreds of a majority in the same constituency. Did the government do anything in the meantime that would entitle them to the confidence of the people of Prince Edward Island, or of anywhere else ? Not at all. It was a corrupt transaction and nothing else. I say that the action of the government in this matter will not be satisfactory to the people of Canada. It may be all right to say to Prince Edward Isand : We give you $30,000 a year, the interest on a million dollars capitalized ; we only give you this as a first instalment, for the alleged nonfulfilment of the terms in regard to efficient steam communication between the island and the mainland. Does the Minister of Mr. FIELDING.
Marine and Fisheries tell us that there was not efficient steam communication ?
The	MINISTER	OF	MARINE	AND
FISHERIES. Yes.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
What has he been doing in these five years to make it right ?
The	MINISTER	OF	MARINE	ANDFISHERIES. Got	a new	steel steamer and
put her on, and made it right; and she runs satisfactorily too.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
Then where are the damages ?
The	MINISTER	OF	MARINE	AND
FISHERIES. The damages are for the many years you did not keep it right. You did not keep your contract.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: What were you doing when you were in before, that you did not keep it ?

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: We kept the contract.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: The minister tells us now that all the difficulties have been removed-that he has put on a new steel vessel. I would like to know where was his efficient steamship when he himself complained that he could not get to Ottawa last winter; and I know that there wrere some others trying to get over to Prince Edward Island.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: My hon. friend wall lay the foundation for another claim if he is not careful.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Having discovered that this is an old claim, how does the hon. gentleman now feel about it ?
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: I presumed that the $30,000 a year for all time to come would cover claims of that kind for the future. It is not a settlement of an old claim at all, because this $30,000 a year is for all time.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: You would sooner pay them $1,000,000, then ?
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
I would sooner the government would come down with some straight proposition instead of a proposition of this kind, which I do not approve of, which is utterly unjustifiable. It is an invitation to the province of Prince Edward Island to prefer further claims, because it is not a settlement of all claims which the province has. It is only the settlement of one question out of a number. The Finance Minister comes with a projjosal to settle that question, which they now tell us is a difficulty of the past, by voting a subsidy for all time to come of $30,000 a year, the interest on $1,000,000, for the purpose of satisfying the people of Prince

Edward Island, because at some time in the past that service was not as efficient as the people of Prince Edward Island thought it should be. The government of Canada, before hon. gentlemen opposite came into power, made the most strenuous efforts to have the navigation between Prince Edward Island and the mainland kept open, and they succeeded very well indeed. We know that members coming here every year had free access to the island, and returned whenever they wanted. I do not remember whether the Minister of Marine and Fisheries was ever delayed until this year; but this year he could not cross to attend to his duties in parliament; this is the year in which we find the greatest difficulty; and yet the government are paying Prince Edward Island an enormous sum of money for the settlement of only one question of the past-not all the points in dispute between the province and the Dominion. Why do they not come down with a complete settlement instead of leaving these other questions open and unsettled ? We have here the province of New Brunswick handing over the railways, and demanding large sums of money from the Dominion government; we have the same thing from the province of Nova Scotia. Presumably we may have a similar demand from the province of Ontario, with a much stronger claim, I should judge, if it should make a claim. But for my part I do not believe in these continual attacks on the purse of the Dominion. This was never contemplated, and it is simply a carrying out of election pledges intended to corrupt the people and have the government returned to power.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
I do not want to prolong the debate or repeat the statement I made the other day; but I really cannot let my hon. friend escape without replying to the statement he last made. Is it true that this is merely carrying out election pledges ? The hon. gentleman knows as well as I do that his late colleague in the government, Senator Ferguson, was the co-leader of the provincial government who pressed this very claim, which we are now settling, harder upon our predecessors and upon the Imperial government than anybody else. It was not a claim kept up by one political party alone. It was a claim which the people of the island thought they had justly, and which was put forward by every successive government since the year 1886, Senator Ferguson and the present Chief Justice Sullivan, who then led the government of. Prince Edward Island, were knocking at the door of parliament and at the door of the Privy Council here for years; and they carried their claim home to the foot of the Throne, and prayed Her Majesty the Queen to do that justice to the province which they said the Dominion government
refused to do. Lord Granville, after listening to both sides, said he regretted that he had not power to interefere with the Dominion government.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: What year was that ?

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: This is all contained in the memorandum. That was in 1886. But Lord Granville recommended to the government that if they had made a contract with Prince Edward Island which it was impossible for them literally to carry out, they might meet it by building a tunnel instead of providing winter communication by steam.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Surely the hon. gentleman does not lay stress on so visionary a suggestion by a gentleman having no power to dictate to Canada ?

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: I do not know what the hon. gentleman means by laying stress; but I am stating what the opinion of Lord Granville was. At that very time, the then High Commissioner, Sir Charles Tupper, intimated that the government would favourably consider the proposal to build a tunnel, if the project was feasible, and a letter was written by the then Prime Minister of Canada, Sir John Macdonald, intimating that he would take steps at once to ascertain whether a tunnel was feasible.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Is that in the correspondence ?

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
The papers were all brought before the House years ago. This is a matter of public history. It was not a matter of party politics. Ask the hon. members from Prince County, east and west, whether the carrying out of election pledges or party politics has anything to do with it. It was a substantial claim which there is not a corporal's guard in Prince Edward Island who do not believe is just, and which has been constantly pressed on this government. No hon. member of this House wants this government to stand in the position of having broken a solemn compact which it has made with one of the provinces, and then saying, we will not pay you a dollar of damages, although we have broken our compact, and you cannot sue us-go and do as you like. Is the smallness of the province a ground upon which you should refuse to settle an honest claim ? Does any one suppose, if the province of Ontario or the province of Quebec had made a compact binding on this Dominion, and it was not carried out, that the representatives of those provinces in the Dominion parliament would not compel it to be carried out ? Its honour, its good faith, is at stake, and that is now being saved by what is a very fair compromise of a long outstanding claim, arising out of the fact that the Dominion

government did not fairly or honestly attempt to carry out its contract for many years, in consequence of which failure the people of the island suffered untold injury.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: It is refreshing to have the hon. gentleman explain the reasons why the claim of the island should he sustained by this government. What is the claim V It is for the non-performance of the terms of the union between the Island and Canada. It is based on the non-carrying out of that part of the contract which provides that there shall be efficient steam service between the island and the mainland.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: No.
speakername: The MINISTER OP MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: How has that contract been broken 1 In the first instance, there was what could hardly be called a service at all, that performed by the steamer Alert. Afterwards there was the service performed by the Northern Light, and the hon. gentleman was accustomed to plead that the Northern Light efficiently did the work. I have often heard the hon. gentleman again and again defend in this House the service of the Northern Light. It was the party of the hon. gentleman, which was in power from 1874 to 1S78, to which was committed the task of carrying out the terms of confederation and seeing that the steam service between the island and the mainland was an efficient one. It was his friends who built the Northern Light, and the Northern Light, did its duty efficiently.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: No.
speakername: The MINISTER OP MARINE AND PISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: It is curious how a few years have altered the hon. gentleman's mind.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: I know that the hon. gentleman does not want to put words into my mouth that I never used. What I said was that the Northern Light's service was an honest and faithful attempt to carry out the compact, but it failed. There was never any doubt of the bona fides of those who built the Northern Light, but for some reason or other, every time the hon. gentleman speaks on this subject, he omits to state fairly the terms of that contract. The contract provided, not merely for efficient communication, but continuous communication. The late government put their construction upon that provision, and they said that efficient communication meant continuous communication between the island and the railways of the mainland.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND PISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
That question of construction has been threshed out again and again. Continuous communication between the island and the mainland meant only such communication as the laws of Sir LOUIS DAVIES.
nature would allow. The doctrine of force majeure applies in the case, as the hon. Minister of Marine well knows. This is a claim on account of the non-performance of that condition when the hon. gentleman and his friends were in power. But what I want to point out is that over and over again the Minister of Marine has argued that the service of the Northern Light was an efficient one.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: You never heard me say so.
speakername: The MINISTER OP MARINE AND PISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
I will read the very words of the hon. gentleman taken from ' Hansard.' They were uttered in reply to Sir John Macdonald :
I rise for the purpose of correcting the hon. gentleman, who two or three times over gave as statements made by me statements which I did not make. I did not say that the Northern Light was quite sufficient for the purpose for which it was built. On the contrary, I explained that in spring and fall it did effective service.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Hear, hear.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: But in the middle of winter, for a period of a month or six weeks, no boat could be built to do the work.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Hear, hear.
speakername: The MINISTER OP MARINE AND PISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
And the hon. gentleman went on to state that it was impossible for any boat to do the work more efficiently for two or three weeks in the year that the Northern Light did it.
I remember the complaints made by Mr. Ferguson and Mr. Sullivan and other hon. gentlemen on our side about the non-efficiency of the service, but that service found no more ardent defender in this House than the present Minister of Marine and Fisheries. Our friends opposite, when in power, had the duty of carrying out the conditions of the contract. It was they who built this steamer, and the hon. minister contended that, with a little improvement, it would do the service efficiently, but that for two or three weeks in the year it was. impossible that that service could be performed by any steamer. He has changed his mind since then. Perhaps modern ideas and enterprise have discovered improvements, which will enable a continuous service to be had between Prince Edward Island and the mainland, but what I rose to observe was that the conditions of the contract were carried out as faithfully as possible with the mechanical appliances available at the time, and that one of those who claimed that it was so carried out is the Minister of Marine.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Not so.
speakername: The MINISTER OP MARINE AND PISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext:
Not only did the succeeding Conservative government perform

the service with the means furnished by lion, gentlemen opposite, but we put on an extra service besides. We subsidized steamers for the purpose of supplementing this service. We gave to parties in Charlottetown and other places large subsidies for a supplementary service.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: Not in winter.
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: During the whole year.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: For summer only.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: As long as they could do it ; as long as the service could be performed. We gave the sum for the purpose of supplementing the service by the Northern Light I am not objecting to the $30,000 a year given to Prince Edward Island, but do not give it on the ground of a claim for which there is no foundation at all. The real claim which Prince Edward Island has against this government is another one. In the financial arrangement, under which that province entered confederation, it did not get the allowance it was entitled to.

maintopic: P. E. I. CLAIMS-MAINTENANCE OF STEAM COMMUNICATION.
speechtext: They will put in a claim for that now.
